newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Tutu needs further cancer therapy.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Tutu needs further cancer therapy.

text.p: South African Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu said on Wednesday his prostate cancer appeared to have spread and he would go to the United States for radiation therapy.
Tutu, 65, a leading campaigner in the fight against apartheid, had most of his prostate cut out in January when the gland was diagnosed as cancerous.
Doctors told him at the time he would need further surgery or treatment with radiation and hormones.

Tutu, now chairman of South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission probing apartheid crimes, said in a statement that after consulting doctors in the United States last week he had decided on a combination of hormone treatment and radiotherapy.
The former archbishop of Cape Town visited two U.S. clinics, Johns Hopkins Medical Centre in Baltimore and the Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Centre in New York.
"I have been advised that the cancer is suspected to have penetrated beyond the prostate gland and that as a result radiotherapy is the best option," he said in a statement.

"Medical specialists in Cape Town will begin a three-month course of hormone treatment tomorrow (Thursday)...After the hormone treatment, I plan to have the radiotherapy at a clinic in the United States," Tutu said. "This will take two months."

He said that while he was in the United States he would set up an office through which he would keep close touch with the truth commission, which is investigating human rights abuses by both sides of the apartheid divide.
Tutu, regarded as the conscience of South Africa, was awarded the Nobel peace prize in 1984 for his efforts to end apartheid.
But he has not hesitated to criticise President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress, which won historic elections in April 1994, over what he sees as its weaknesses or failings.
Tutu said on Wednesday he hoped to follow a normal schedule during the hormone treatment in Cape Town "but will be unable to continue squeezing additional commitments in the schedule".
